people.label: Cecilia Levy
people.sub: Associate Professor of Physics, University at Albany (SUNY); LZ dark-matter physicist; third UAlbany author on the 2025 UAPx field-expedition paper
people.narrative: Cecilia Levy is the third University at Albany physicist on the only peer-reviewed UAP field-expedition paper published to date, and she is on this board for a narrow and checkable reason: the University named her, in its own press release, as one of three 'UAlbany authors' on Szydagis, Knuth, Kugielsky & Levy (2025). Her career is otherwise entirely conventional astroparticle physics. She took a BSc at the Universite de Montreal, an MSc at Queen's University on the PICASSO dark matter experiment, a PhD at the University of Muenster on XENON100, a postdoc at RPI on XENON1T, and a postdoc at Albany on LUX/LZ, and she is now an Associate Professor in the same department as Szydagis and Knuth. Her stated research is the direct detection of dark matter: she works on the seven-tonne LZ detector at the Sanford Underground Research Facility, where her group handled detector cleanliness and the 206Pb wall background, and she co-develops the Snowball Chamber, a supercooled-water low-mass dark matter detector she describes as 'a research topic completely unique to the UAlbany dark matter group'. She co-authored the founding Snowball Chamber paper with Szydagis in 2018. That shared instrument work is the mechanism by which rare-event detection practice reached the UAP field campaign: the University's release explains that Szydagis's C-TAP frame-differencing software applies an approach 'used by physicists like him and Levy to look for direct evidence of dark matter'. One honest qualification belongs on the record. Unlike Szydagis, whose departmental page lists Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena among his research interests, Levy's faculty page makes no mention of UAP at all. Her involvement is visible in the publication and in the press office, not in her declared research profile - which is a reasonable description of how most working scientists have touched this subject.

entities.label: Knuth et al. (2025), 'The New Science of Unidentified Aerospace-Undersea Phenomena (UAP)', Progress in Aerospace Sciences
entities.sub: 34-author review of UAP studies 1933-present; Knuth lead author, Szydagis co-author
entities.desc: The companion piece to the UAPx field-expedition paper in the same Progress in Aerospace Sciences special edition, and the larger of the two. UAlbany's news office describes it as 'a comprehensive review of studies conducted on UAPs from 1933 to the present, including more than 20 historical government and privately funded projects as well as recent scientific research efforts in Ireland, France, Germany, Norway, Sweden and the United States', with Knuth as lead author 'co-written by Szydagis and more than 30 other researchers from around the world'. SCU's June 2025 press release puts the author count at thirty-four and gives the DOI as 10.1016/j.paerosci.2025.101097. Its stated aims, per the University, are to clarify the historical scientific narrative, to establish that UAP have been observed and recorded for well over 150 years and studied by astronomers, scientists and engineers, and to show that several serious academic efforts in multiple countries are currently collecting instrumented data. Its significance for this board is structural rather than evidentiary: a thirty-four-author review in a high-impact aerospace engineering journal, led from a state university physics department, is the closest thing the subject has to a conventional field-defining literature review, and it exists because two faculty members at a mid-sized SUNY campus were willing to put their names on it.

entities.label: SOYUZUFOTSENTR - USSR Inter-Industry Ufology Research Centre
entities.sub: 1990 Soviet ufology centre with USSR Academy of Sciences institute rights, headed by V. G. Azhazha; named in UK Project Condign
entities.desc: CORRECTED NODE - previously a bookkeeping stub with a null description and no sources. SOYUZUFOTSENTR is on this board because a UK Defence Intelligence Staff report classified SECRET UK EYES ONLY thought it worth naming. Project Condign Volume 3, Chapter 4 records that a 'UFO' Commission was created under the USSR Union of Scientific and Engineering Societies in 1989, and that in 1990 an Inter-Industry Ufology Research Centre - Condign transliterates it SOYUZUFOSENTR - was created to co-ordinate records; that the centre held the rights of an Institute under the USSR Academy of Sciences; and that it was headed by V. G. Azhazha, 'an eminent researcher and former naval submariner'. Condign records a ten-week school with terms of reference to study 'ufology as a science of unidentified flying objects and their interrelations with the universe and, in particular, with the biotechnosphere of the earth'; that the Institute developed light filters, instrumentation and IR and UV photography; and that claimed imagery of 'peculiar spheres, humanoid figures' was reported but, in Condign's dry formulation, 'if the imagery exists, it has never been published'. The centre sits at the hinge between the closed Soviet state effort and the open Russian ufology of the 1990s: it was founded in 1990, the year the SETKA programmes ended, and it was the first Soviet UFO organisation to operate publicly. It should NOT be confused with the KLAS-TV / George Knapp document story. Knapp's 1993 Moscow acquisition came from the Ministry of Defence via Colonel Boris Sokolov; the KGB 'Blue Folder' associated with Popovich and Azhazha is a separate collection. That distinction is why the obvious media edge from this node cannot be written.

entities.label: University at Albany (SUNY), Department of Physics
entities.sub: Academic home of Kevin Knuth, Matthew Szydagis and Cecilia Levy; source of both 2025 Progress in Aerospace Sciences UAP papers
entities.desc: CORRECTED NODE - description updated to add Cecilia Levy, the second 2025 paper, and the departmental research-interest listing. The physics department at the University at Albany is, improbably, the most productive academic base in this field outside Stanford and Harvard. It employs Kevin Knuth - information physicist, former NASA Ames research scientist and Editor-in-Chief of Entropy since 2012, on the faculty since 2005 and a full professor since 2023 - along with Matthew Szydagis, a liquid-xenon dark-matter physicist who created the Noble Element Simulation Technique used across the direct-detection community, and Cecilia Levy, an LZ physicist and Szydagis's co-developer on the Snowball Chamber. What makes the institution more than an address is that the commitment is on the record in the department's own materials: Szydagis's faculty page lists 'Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena' among his research interests, and the University's news office published the June 2025 field results under its own masthead, naming the three as 'UAlbany authors' and reporting the honest outcome that the team 'succeeded in plausibly explaining all but one of the potential anomalies detected'. Two papers came out of the same Progress in Aerospace Sciences special edition: the UAPx field-expedition results and Knuth's 34-author review, 'The New Science of Unidentified Aerospace-Undersea Phenomena (UAP)'. Knuth also produced the 2019 Entropy kinematics paper on the Nimitz encounter, and in June 2025 received SCU's inaugural Distinguished Scholar Award. That a mid-sized state university supplies a meaningful fraction of the world's peer-reviewed UAP instrumentation output is a measure of how little institutional capacity exists. Note that UAlbany is not the host or funder of UAPx - the field work was funded by Caroline Cory of OMnium Media for the documentary 'A Tear in the Sky' (2022).

recommend_removal.reason: Incidental biography, on exactly the precedent that removed 31 other locations. Nothing that matters to this subject demonstrably happens in Albany. The city's entire content on this board is the mailing address of the University at Albany. Every locatable event in the Albany cluster occurs elsewhere: the UAPx field expedition behind the only peer-reviewed field-instrumentation result was at Laguna Beach, California (2021); the Nimitz encounter analysed in the 2019 Entropy paper was off southern California (2004); Szydagis's LZ detector work is at the Sanford Underground Research Facility in Lead, South Dakota; SCU's Distinguished Scholar Award was presented in Huntsville, Alabama (June 2025). Contrast l-moscow, which is retained because a Kremlin decision, an MoD institute and IZMIRAN all sit there and the SETKA programme was run from it. Albany has one institution, no event, no decision and no custody transfer. Two further defects support removal: (1) the node's only claim is tier 3 and is an editorial judgement ('the small existing proof that instrumented UAP research can be conducted ... under normal academic norms'), not a fact about a place; (2) its single edge, university-at-albany -> l-albany, is typed 'research' although it describes a containment relationship and its label describes people rather than a place - if the node is retained against this recommendation, that edge must be re-typed 'geographic' and re-labelled. The subject-matter content the node currently carries is not lost: it has been folded into the corrected university-at-albany description.
